name: Build provenance attestations
description: What the build attested about the artifacts it produced, read from the in-toto statements it already wrote (bare or inside a DSSE envelope) and recorded exactly as each document states it. Nothing here verifies a signature.

reports.description: Comma separated globs matched against every file in the working directory and against bare file names, naming the attestations to read.

facts.source: `report` when an attestation was read, `none` when there was none.
facts.reason: Why nothing was read, present only when `source` is `none`.
facts.reports: Every file that was read, in path order. One file can carry several attestations.
facts.reports[].path: Path of the file, relative to the directory the CLI runs in.
facts.reports[].modified: When it was last written, ISO 8601, so an attestation older than the build is recognisable.
facts.reports[].format: Format it was read as, always `intoto`.
facts.counts.total: Attestations across every file that was read.
facts.counts.signed: Attestations that arrived inside a DSSE envelope. The envelope is recorded, never verified, so this counts attestations carrying a signature rather than attestations whose signature was checked.
facts.attestations[].predicateType: What the statement claims to be, such as `https://slsa.dev/provenance/v1`, or `null` when it names none.
facts.attestations[].builder: Identity the statement gives the builder that produced the subjects, or `null` when it names none.
facts.attestations[].sourceUri: Source the statement says was built, or `null` when it names none.
facts.attestations[].sourceDigest: Digest of that source, or `null` when the statement carries none.
facts.attestations[].subjects: The artifacts the statement is about.
facts.attestations[].subjects[].name: Name the statement gives the artifact, empty when it gives none.
facts.attestations[].subjects[].digest: Digest of the artifact, by algorithm, as the statement carries it.
facts.attestations[].envelope: `true` when the statement arrived inside a DSSE envelope, `false` when it arrived bare.
